summary: Evaluation of 14 days of Nightscout telemetry and AAPS profile settings shows an overall Time in Range of 86.0% with strong closed-loop automation. However, mild overnight lows (5.1% time below range) and afternoon postprandial hyperglycemia peaks occur. The user does not log carbohydrates (`carb_entries: 0`), relying entirely on UAM and closed-loop micro-bolusing.

analysis_steps.findings: High CGM data coverage (98.7%) across 14 days with 10 minor gaps. Telemetry completeness is strong, though zero carbohydrate entries are recorded.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3,995 valid entries out of 4,046 expected; 2,315 treatments and 6,214 device statuses.

analysis_steps.findings: Average glucose is 121.6 mg/dL with 86.0% TIR. Time below range is 5.1%, indicating mild hypoglycemia frequency that requires conservative insulin adjustments.
analysis_steps.evidence: 16 glucose extremes below 70 mg/dL (dropping to 41-42 mg/dL) and peaks up to 290 mg/dL.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight basal delivery shows mild dips into the 90s mg/dL local hours 00:00-02:00 (TBR up to 18.5%). Afternoon peaks reflect unannounced meal impacts or mismatched sensitivity.
analysis_steps.evidence: Hourly local glucose averages show overnight stability with early-morning low tendencies and afternoon rises.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absence of meal announcements prevents isolating CR versus basal effects.

analysis_steps.findings: Authoritative profile uses a flat 56 mg/dL/U ISF, variable CR segments (10.5-13.2 g/U), and a 10-hour DIA. Closed-loop dynamic sensitivity actively compensates for static settings.
analysis_steps.evidence: Profile definitions combined with active loop telemetry showing variable sensitivity ratios.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of declared carb entries limits empirical CR verification.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are enabled and functioning effectively to manage postprandial glucose in the absence of manual meal entries.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled=true, uam_enabled=true, smb_always_enabled=true, with frequent UAM-driven micro-bolus triggers in loop logs.

analysis_steps.findings: Max IOB (25 U) is set significantly higher than necessary given a ~20 U/day total daily dose. Dynamic ISF (70%) and UAM successfully bridge conservative profile settings.
analysis_steps.evidence: aaps_profile.smb_settings raw settings and loop telemetry max IOB observations.

analysis_steps.findings: In the absence of manual carb entries, the system relies exclusively on UAM and closed-loop adjustments, which maintains good TIR but permits afternoon postprandial excursions.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of explicit meal bolus timing data.

analysis_steps.findings: E-carbs are not utilized. A 7-hour max absorption model appropriately accommodates slow digestion patterns and GLP-1 therapy effects.
analysis_steps.evidence: meal_max_absorption_hours = 7 h and noted GLP-1 1.25mg administration dates.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No explicit extended carb or e-carb records.

analysis_steps.findings: Profile settings and automation parameters are performing adequately to achieve 86% TIR. Changes should be withheld until carb logging habits are established, with a conservative reduction in max IOB recommended for safety.
analysis_steps.evidence: Consistent synthesis across data quality, safety, basal, and automation audits.

strengths: High Time in Range (86.0%) across the 14-day evaluation period.
Excellent CGM data capture (98.7% coverage) and stable glycemic variability (CV 32.6%).
Effective closed-loop automation (SMB/UAM/Dynamic ISF) successfully maintaining control despite zero manual carbohydrate entries.
issues: Mild elevation in time below range (5.1%), with 16 recorded glucose extremes dropping below 70 mg/dL.
Afternoon postprandial hyperglycemia peaks (local hours 15:00-17:00 reaching up to 32.1% time above range).
Absence of manual carbohydrate logging (`carb_entries: 0`), forcing complete reliance on UAM automation.

recommendations.title: Review Max IOB Safety Limit
recommendations.description: Max IOB is currently set to 25 U, which is significantly higher than the user's total daily dose (~20 U/day). Lowering this ceiling reduces risk during loop anomalies while remaining well above normal operational IOB.

recommendations.title: Monitor Overnight Basal and Early Morning Lows
recommendations.description: Overnight glucose shows dips into the 90s mg/dL with early-morning time below range reaching up to 18.5%. Observe whether slight adjustments to 00:00 basal are needed after establishing meal logging.

profile_recommendation.rationale: Current profile basal segments, ISF, CR, and target values maintain a strong 86% TIR. Because carbohydrates are not manually logged and dynamic sensitivity is active, altering static profile parameters without baseline meal data is premature.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Record explicit carbohydrate amounts for at least 3 to 5 meals over the next week to evaluate postprandial response before modifying profile CR or ISF segments.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep current profile settings unchanged while initiating trial manual carbohydrate logging.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Overnight glucose is generally stable, and any minor dips are managed by loop automation. Evidence does not justify altering basal without meal-logging context.
Current rate maintains stable early morning trends. Dependency on GLP-1 timing suggests withholding changes.
Morning basal supports waking glucose rise. Keep current pending meal-logging data.
Midday basal segment operates stably with dynamic ISF adjustments.
Afternoon peaks are driven by unannounced meal absorption rather than basal insufficiency.
Evening basal segment maintains appropriate evening stability.
Nighttime transition basal is well-supported by current loop behavior.
Without explicit carbohydrate entries, CR efficacy cannot be empirically recalculated.
Keep current until meal logging provides data to evaluate ratio performance.
Morning CR segment performs adequately under UAM automation.
Afternoon CR matches observed postprandial containment by UAM.
Evening CR segment maintains stable overnight transitions.
Flat ISF of 56 mg/dL/U paired with Dynamic ISF (70%) provides safe, conservative insulin sensitivity scaling.
Target of 90 mg/dL supports tight control without excessive hypoglycemia.
Daytime target of 100 mg/dL is appropriate and safe.
Late evening target maintains smooth overnight entry.
Conservative 10-hour DIA prevents insulin stacking and aligns with closed-loop safety.
Essential for managing unannounced meals and maintaining 86% TIR.
Appropriately configured to support UAM micro-bolusing given zero declared carb entries.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Deliveries are functioning smoothly without evidence of aggressive insulin stacking.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Max basal is safe. Max IOB of 25 U is high relative to TDD (~20 U/day) but requires careful verification before alteration.
Dynamic ISF at 70% successfully scales sensitivity and compensates for conservative profile ISF.
7-hour max absorption correctly accommodates slow digestion and GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain UAM-driven closed-loop automation (`smb_enabled=true`, `uam_enabled=true`, `smb_always_enabled=true`) with the 7-hour absorption model. Introduce manual carbohydrate logging and pre-meal bolusing for known meals to reduce afternoon postprandial excursions.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: In the absence of manual carbohydrate entries (`total_carbs_g = 0.0`), AAPS successfully maintains an 86.0% Time in Range using UAM and Dynamic ISF. However, unannounced meal detection results in delayed postprandial containment.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Record explicit carbohydrate amounts for 3 to 5 meals over the next week to evaluate whether manual meal bolusing improves postprandial stability.

exceptions.suggestion: Maintain conservative max IOB and allow the 7-hour absorption window to handle delayed digestion.
exceptions.rationale: GLP-1 receptor agonists significantly slow gastric emptying, extending carbohydrate absorption profiles.

implementation_steps: Step 1: Review current safety limits and discuss lowering max IOB closer to operational needs with the care team.
Step 2: Initiate trial manual carbohydrate logging for a subset of meals to establish baseline CR and prebolus efficacy.
Step 3: Monitor postprandial glucose trajectories and hypoglycemia frequency before considering profile segment changes.
education: Unannounced Meal (UAM) detection allows AAPS to micro-bolus when glucose momentum rises, but manual carbohydrate entry significantly improves postprandial peak control.
GLP-1 receptor agonists delay gastric absorption, making extended absorption windows (such as 7 hours) essential for preventing late postprandial stacking.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
